subject: Expansion pricing for new payments workloads — add-on commit and per-token tiers
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@stellarpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@stellarpay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Expanding usage — pricing for new Fraud-ML and reconciliation pipelines

Jordan — thanks again for the demo last week. We’ve got internal buy-in to expand Redwood to two additional workloads: a near-real-time fraud inference path (high QPS, short responses) and a daily reconciliation batch that will consume high embedding volume for record matching.

High level asks:
- We plan to add ~200M tokens/month across both workloads in the first quarter of production, ramping to ~1B tokens/month over 6–9 months if accuracy and latency hold.
- We need a predictable committed spend for finance but want usage-based rollback for burst months. Can you outline how incremental commit tiers + per-token discounts would work?
- Any special pricing for embeddings vs. chat/generation? Embedding usage will be ~60% of token volume.

Happy to share rough usage patterns if that helps model a proposal. Can we get a ballpark by EOW?

— Emily
Emily Park
Head of Platform Integrations, StellarPay
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@stellarpay.com>
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Expanding usage — pricing for new Fraud-ML and reconciliation pipelines

Thanks Emily — congrats on the internal greenlight. I can get a draft pricing structure to you by Friday. A couple quick asks to narrow options: can you share current monthly token baseline for the teams we already run (approx tokens/month)? Also:
- Do you expect the fraud path to be latency-sensitive (p95 target <= 250ms)?
- Are embeddings being stored / indexed by StellarPay or will Redwood host vector store / cache?

If you prefer, Rajesh and I can do a 20-min call Monday to review rough numbers — that usually gives us enough to propose sensible breakpoints.

I’ll route a preliminary add-on commit proposal to our commercial team and loop in Marissa for customer-specific discounts.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: StellarPay expansion — need pricing guidance (embeddings-heavy)

Marissa / Aditya — forwarding StellarPay note. Key things: 200M tokens/month initial, 1B tokens/month target; ~60% embeddings; fraud path is latency-sensitive. They want a committed spend that finance can predict but with some protection for burst months.

Can you propose:
1) A 12-month add-on commit SKU (tokens/month) with 3 breakpoints (200M, 500M, 1B) and associated per-token discounts.
2) Terms for unused commit credits (rollover, credits, or refund?).
3) Any special guidance for embeddings pricing vs. generation (we typically discount embeddings when they’re vectorized at scale).

I’ve attached last month’s usage report from their trial (usage_report_May2027.csv) and our canonical breakpoints spreadsheet (RI_usage_breakpoints_May2027.xlsx).

Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: StellarPay expansion — need pricing guidance (embeddings-heavy)

Jordan — drafting options below. I recommend we present two flavors: Commit-first (bigger discount) and Hybrid (commit + overage at tiered rate). Also note legal will want clear language around unused credits and auditability.

Option A — 12m Add-on Commit (commit covers both workloads)
- Breakpoints: 200M / 500M / 1B tokens per month
- Per-token effective rate (generation): $0.0006 / $0.00045 / $0.00035 respectively
- Embeddings: additional 20% reduction off the generation rate at each breakpoint (applies when embeddings > 40% of monthly tokens)
- Overage: 110% of per-token rate for usage beyond commit; bursts above 1.5x handled via temporary burst capacity (billed at 150% rate)
- Unused credits: rollover up to 3 months, then expire; finance can purchase one-time 6m carry-forward for 5% fee

Option B — Hybrid 12m (smaller commit + usage tiering)
- Commit: 200M tokens/month minimum (guaranteed), incremental usage billed at tiered rates with softer discounts: $0.00075 / $0.00055 / $0.00040
- Embeddings: flat $0.00030 per embedding token after commit is consumed (this preserves predictability for recon workloads)
- Unused credits: no rollover; credits applied to overage before billing at list rates

Commercial notes:
- We can offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of the first 3 months’ commit if they sign within 21 days.
- Proposed SLA/latency guarantee for fraud path: we can commit to p95 <= 250ms for dedicated capacity (Dedicated pool add-on); if they want hosted without dedicated, we recommend a fallback model and slightly higher p95 target.

I’ll attach a sample SOW skeleton and suggested Mutual Action Plan (Doc in Drive). Let me know if you want these numbers softened for an exec ask — otherwise I’ll send to Emily for feedback.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial | Redwood Inference
From: Emily Park <emily.park@stellarpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
Cc: Rajesh Kumar <rajesh.kumar@stellarpay.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing for new Fraud-ML and reconciliation pipelines — clarifications

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the speedy options. A few clarifying questions before we show to finance: 
1) If we select Option A and hit only 400M tokens/month (below the 500M breakpoint), does the company pay the 500M rate? Or do we get pro-rated pricing?
2) For embeddings: can you confirm the 20% discount applies to the per-token charge for embedding calls (not per-vector index cost) — we want to ensure monthly storage/indexing costs are separate.
3) Unused credits: rollover up to 3 months is reasonable; finance will ask for a cap on total rollover (we’d prefer not to see credits expire for a 1–2yr commercial relationship).

Also, curious whether Redwood will allow a mid-term top-up to move us up a breakpoint without re-signing a full 12m. That flexibility could make the hybrid plan easier for us.

If you can confirm those items, we can put a target of getting a draft SOW to procurement by next Wed.

— Emily
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@stellarpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Expansion pricing for new Fraud-ML and reconciliation pipelines — clarifications

Emily — answers inline below. I’ve attached the SOW draft and our breakpoints workbook for your procurement team to review (Stellar_SOW_draft.pdf, RI_usage_breakpoints_May2027.xlsx).

1) Breakpoint billing: If you choose Option A and actual usage is 400M that month, you are charged at the 200M or 500M tier based on which commit you select. We recommend matching the commit to expected monthly usage and using our mid-term top-up (see #4) to move to the next breakpoint. We do not auto-charge at higher tier rates if usage is below the selected commit; the commit is a contracted monthly token allocation priced at that tier.

2) Embeddings discount: confirmed — the 20% reduction applies to the per-token call rate for embedding generation. Storage and index hosting (if you use Redwood-managed vector store) are billed separately on a monthly storage/ops line item in the SOW.

3) Rollover cap: we can set a floor such that rollover is capped at 2x the monthly commit (so excess beyond that expires). For strategic deals we can extend to 3x with an enterprise amendment; I’ll flag that as an escalation item if procurement pushes back.

4) Mid-term top-up: yes — we support an asynchronous top-up flow. Customer can purchase an instantaneous bump to the commit to move to the next breakpoint; the new tier pricing takes effect immediately and the balance is pro-rated for the remaining months in the term. No need to re-sign the whole 12m SOW.

Next steps: if these are acceptable I’ll convert the SOW to a DocuSign-ready version and loop in Legal for a quick redline window. Targeting procurement review by Wed as you requested.

Jordan Blake
Principal Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.example | +1 (415) 555-0123
